'''Jonathan Peter Keating''' {{post-nominals|country=GBR|FRS}} (born 20 September 1963) is a British mathematician. As of September 2019, he is the [[Sedleian Professor of Natural Philosophy]] at the [[University of Oxford]], and from 2012 to 2019 was the Henry Overton Wills Professor of Mathematics at the [[University of Bristol]], where he served as Dean of the Faculty of Science (2009–2013).  He has made contributions to [[applied mathematics]] and [[mathematical physics]], in particular to [[quantum chaos]], [[random matrix theory]] and [[number theory]].

==Education==
He read for an MA in physics at [[New College, Oxford]], before obtaining his PhD in 1989 at the [[University of Bristol]] supervised by [[Michael Berry (physicist)|Michael Berry]].<ref name=mathgene/><ref>[https://www.bristol.ac.uk/maths/people/jon-p-keating/index.html Jon P. Keating Website at the University of Bristol]</ref>

==Research and career==
{{BLP sources section|date=April 2021}}
He lectured in [[applied mathematics]] at the [[University of Manchester]] from 1991 to 1995 before moving to the [[University of Bristol]], as a reader in [[applied mathematics]] (1995–1997) and then as a professor in [[mathematical physics]] (1997–2012). He served as head of the Mathematics department (2001–2004) and was appointed to the Henry Overton Wills Chair in Mathematics at Bristol in 2012.  His research has focused on [[quantum chaos]], [[random matrix theory]] and its connection to [[number theory]], especially the theory of the [[Riemann zeta-function]] and other [[L-function]]s. He is known for his work on the resummation of semiclassical periodic orbit formulae, the statistics of quantum energy levels, quantum maps, [[quantum graph]]s, the statistics of the [[zero of a function|zeros]] of the [[Riemann zeta-function]] and other {{nowrap|[[L-functions]]}}, and the moments of the Riemann zeta-function and other {{nowrap|L-functions}}.  He has served on the editorial boards of several [[peer review]]ed [[scientific journal]]s including:

* Member (1996–2004) of the editorial board of ''Journal of Physics A''. 
* Member (1997–2004) of the editorial board of ''[[Nonlinearity_(journal) | Nonlinearity]]''.
* Joint Editor-in-Chief (2004–2012) of ''Nonlinearity''.
* Member (2003–2017) of the editorial board of ''Applied Mathematics Research Express''.
* Member (2007–present) of the editorial board of ''[[Journal of Mathematical Physics]]''.

He was the Chair of the [[Heilbronn Institute for Mathematical Research]] until July 2020.

In September 2019, he succeeded [[John M. Ball]] as [[Sedleian Professor of Natural Philosophy]] at the [[University of Oxford]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.maths.ox.ac.uk/node/31418|title=Jon Keating appointed to the Sedleian Professorship of Natural Philosophy|work=University of Oxford}}</ref>

In November 2019 he succeeded [[Caroline Series]] as president of the [[London Mathematical Society]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.lms.ac.uk/news-entry/29062018-1719/lms-president-designate|title=LMS President Designate|work=London Mathematical Society}}</ref>

His doctoral students include [[Nina Snaith]].<ref name=mathgene>{{MathGenealogy}}</ref><ref name=PhDsniath>{{cite thesis|degree=PhD|publisher=University of Bristol|title=Random matrix theory and zeta functions|first= Nina Claire|last=Snaith|date=2000|id={{EThOS|uk.bl.ethos.322610}}|oclc=53552484}}</ref>

==Awards and honours==
Between 2004 and 2009 Keating was supported by an EPSRC Senior Research Fellowship.

He was elected a [[Fellow of the Royal Society]] (FRS) in 2009.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://royalsociety.org/about-us/fellowship/fellows/|title=Fellows|work=The Royal Society}}</ref>

In 2010, he was awarded the London Mathematical Society's [[Fröhlich Prize]].<ref>[https://www.lms.ac.uk/sites/lms.ac.uk/files/About_Us/news/2010-06%20LMS%20Prizes%20(2%20July).pdf London Mathematical Society Prizes 2010]</ref>

In 2014, he was awarded a [[Royal Society Wolfson Research Merit Award]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://royalsociety.org/news/2014/wolfson-merit-awards-may|title=Royal Society announces new round of esteemed Wolfson Research Merit Awards|work=The Royal Society}}</ref>

He holds an ERC Advanced Grant.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://logcorrm.blogs.ilrt.org|title=LogCorrM}}</ref>
